text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000009 bills 99215 well above expectation in every complexity band, including many low-complexity visits, but the sampled charts largely support the billed levels, so the picture is unresolved.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The elevated 99215 share is not concentrated in sicker patients. It appears in the 0- and 1-condition bands too, and sampled 99215s include simple presentations such as upper respiratory infection (C0003110, C0003224), follow-up visits (C0003291, C0003292) and abdominal pain (C0003312), which is the pattern of concern. Against that, the documented 99215 claims rarely fall below the billed level, well under the comparison rate, and on the face of the charts this argues for a legitimately complex panel. Even so, high-MDM notes on simple visits such as C0003224 (J06.9) and C0003090 (N39.0) are clinically surprising. Together with the frequent problem-list note signal, the handful of moderate-plus data claims with no lab or test line, and the missing audit trail, this leaves open the possibility that notes are templated or inflated to match the billed code, though it does not establish it. A reviewer should first pull the full notes for the supported low-complexity 99215s (C0003090, C0003193, C0003224, C0003455) and the problem-signal examples, and judge whether the documented MDM is clinically credible for the stated diagnosis. The reviewer should also request the EHR audit trail to check for cloning or bulk note creation before drawing a conclusion."}
